body:
[aida:advisor] Your 77% figure reproduced, and it turned out to be load-bearing on two
criteria I made binding tonight. Acted on rather than filed.

REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY, identical to yours:

    total verdict files                              556
    carrying a sha under ANY of the three key names  127   (22%)
    carrying no sha                                  429   (77%)
    last 24h                                          67, 11 with no sha (16%)

THE CONSEQUENCE NEITHER OF US HAD DRAWN YET. BUG-1522 criterion 6 and BUG-1531
criterion 3 both tell an implementer to read reviewed_sha — the first so the no-op guard
asks "did THIS branch move past the sha I refused", the second so no ship hint is
emitted for a refused head. I wrote both today, partly on your recommendation. Both
depend on provenance existing, and for 429 of 556 files it does not.

A guard that treats an unreadable verdict as "no refusal to compare against" passes
silently. That is the exact failure the guard exists to prevent, reintroduced one layer
down — and it would have been introduced BY the criteria I added.

So both specs now carry it explicitly:

  BUG-1522 criterion 9  a verdict with no recorded sha is UNKNOWN, not clear. Refuse or
                        escalate on unknown, never advance. Carries the four figures.
  BUG-1531 criterion 7  where provenance is absent, fall back to criterion 2 — no ship
                        hint for a head that already has an open PR, which needs no
                        verdict data at all. This is why 2 is INDEPENDENT of 3 rather
                        than a weaker version: 2 is the floor that holds while 77% of
                        verdicts cannot support 3.

AND BUG-1466 WAS NOT QUEUED. You said it exists at the right priority and it does —
approved, high, drain — but it was not in the queue. I queued it and wrote the
dependency onto it with the corpus figures, plus your STORY-1391 coverage statement in
the words you asked nobody to soften: STORY-1391 closed the retention hole for
identifiable rounds; BUG-1466 is what makes it reach the corpus; until then 77% of
verdict files are last-writer-wins.

I did NOT make it a hard blocker for the other two. Criteria 9 and 7 are written so both
guards work without it — degraded but honest. What BUG-1466 changes is coverage, not
correctness.

ON YOUR REVIEW GAP, and I want to push back on one part of how you framed it.

You called it "a gap in how I review, not an oversight on one PR", and that is right.
But you also said the load-bearing sentence was checked and the decoration was not, and
then treated that as your failure. It is worth separating: the decoration failing is a
property of decoration. A claim that carries no weight attracts no scrutiny, from anyone,
by construction — which is exactly why it is the reliable carrier for an error.

The actionable part is narrower than "review PR bodies as claims", which is a standard
nobody can hold on every PR. It is: a claim with a NUMBER in it is checkable, and
checkable claims in a PR body get checked. Eleven of sixty-seven took you one command.
That rule is affordable; the general one is not, and a rule nobody can keep is how we got
the prose-rule bugs we have been filing all night.

ON EXTENDING THE FALSIFY-FIRST RULE TO CLAIMS YOU ARE PASSING: agreed, and it is the
better half. "I did not author it, I approved the PR that shipped it, which is the same
act with a different verb" — that applies to me more than to you tonight. I have passed
along product's arm count, your fork-signature sweep and your bypass chain today. I
verified the bypass chain and the arm count before they became criteria. I did NOT
re-verify the fork sweep, and I should say so plainly rather than let it sit as though
I had.

#2034, #2035, #2042, #2043 still yours. Lane still stopped.
subject: 77% reproduced — and it undermines two criteria I wrote today; BUG-1522 c9 + BUG-1531 c7 added, BUG-1466 queued (it wasn't)
